parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile national layer with a comparatively restrained state. Visitor-facing exposures are engineered at entry (Feb 2025 cable directing refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, possible fraud/lifetime-ineligibility finding; X markers ended), federally funded single-sex facilities barred to trans people, and documented abuse in immigration custody (forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse). The state itself is in a July 2026 'low-risk' group, vetoed bathroom bills, and offers employment/public-accommodation protections in nine cities. Offsetting negatives: no state gender-identity hate-crime coverage, available trans-panic defence, a minors' surgery/sports ban, and Pride dissolution. No documented state violence, but absence is not safety.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable instructs officers to refuse where documents or records cast reasonable doubt on sex, and to consider fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; X markers no longer issued; travellers report passports blocked/confiscated.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements, is never automatic, and limited waivers exist; suit by civil-liberties union pending.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal or secondary screening can escalate to detention, where documented custody abuses apply.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans men in immigration custody report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal) from 2026.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several executive orders blocked or enjoined; consular/legal-aid FAQ maintained.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy at entry can move a traveller into the custody system where these practices operate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; map shows bans in a growing number of states (9+1 all-government buildings).
federal_state_facilities.protection: Governor vetoed state bathroom and pronoun bills in June 2023; no facility ban documented for this state.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility exclusion reaches visitors in national buildings regardless of the state's protective posture.

care_services.exposure: State bars sex-reassignment surgery on transgender children (2023); 1982 Medicaid surgery exclusion unresolved; federal orders restrict minors' care and insurance reimbursement.
care_services.protection: June 2023 executive order grants state employees over 21 full gender-affirming coverage; August 2024 order permits birth-certificate change without surgery.
care_services.interaction: A family travelling with a trans minor may face restricted or refused care; adult emergency care unaffected in the record.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders describe minors' care as 'mutilation', direct law enforcement to investigate 'gender ideology'; counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; hospital records subpoenaed; state hotline to report 'gender ideology' in schools.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Federal strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target people who merely disagree; several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Heightened official framing raises outing probability and social hostility at every journey stage.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans trans children from female sports and bars surgery on children; federal orders threaten prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition and restrict youth care; passport marker rules apply to minors' documents.
minors_guardians.protection: Assessment says youth policies judged unlikely to extend to adults; governor vetoed school safe-space and pronoun bills.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family may face care refusal for a child and marker-mismatch scrutiny at entry for the whole family.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime statute omits gender identity; gay/trans panic defence available at common law; Pride organising dissolved in the second-largest city in 2026.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute has covered gender identity since 2009; national Title VII and municipal non-discrimination ordinances in nine cities operate.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin state-level recourse weakens remedies if an assault occurs, though national coverage partially fills the gap.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport and executive-order challenges unresolved; Medicaid/coverage interaction and post-2024 birth-certificate litigation status unstated; no documented state violence record, which proves nothing.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ, pending litigation, several orders blocked, and the state's placement in a July 2026 low-risk group.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Outcomes depend on which measures are in force at the moment of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor combines birth-sex prison placement with a cross-dressing crime enabling arrests in administrative buildings and slow remedies. Our state documents no facility ban, no trans-specific offence, and a governor who vetoed bathroom bills — so it sits well above this tier-1/tier-2 profile, despite comparable custody concerns at the federal level.

Similar: extended secondary screening, discretionary entry refusal, administrative outcomes, slow appeals. Ours rates lower because the screening directive is formalised (mandatory refusal on sex doubt plus possible lifetime ineligibility), federally funded facility exclusion is a standing universal exposure, and immigration custody carries documented abuse.

That anchor has trained, respectful border officers, recognised trans-marker passports, written detention reasons, counsel access and compensation. Ours has the opposite document policy, refusal directives, and abused custody — it cannot approach this level, even with the state's protective equality ordinances.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller experiences one system: a national layer that engineers discovery (document/entry directives, federally funded facility exclusion, custody abuse, hostile official framing) sitting on a state that largely refrains from targeting adults, with employment and municipal protections, vetoed bathroom bills, and no documented trans-directed violence here. The state's protections do not neutralise federal entry, facility or custody rules, but they do mean the everyday street, service and policing environment is materially better than the national picture. Offsetting state negatives — no gender-identity hate-crime coverage, available panic defence, minors' care and sports bans, Pride collapse — are real but secondary to the federal exposures. Absence of a state violence record is not safety.
